chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Umar ibn Arafa, who said:

I heard Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying: 'You must enjoin the good and forbid the evil, or else your wicked ones will be appointed over you; then your good ones will supplicate, but their supplication will not be answered for them.'
ai.seo_question: What is the consequence of neglecting enjoining good and forbidding evil according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi underscores the communal obligation (fard kifaya) of enjoining good and forbidding evil, warning that neglect leads to the rise of the 'evil ones' (shirar) whose authority renders the supplications of the 'good ones' (khayar) ineffective. In Shia scholarship, this is often interpreted as a causal link between societal moral decay and the veiling of divine response, highlighting the critical role of active moral enforcement in maintaining spiritual vitality.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Umar Bin Arafa who said,

‘I heard Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘You should be enjoining with the good and should be forbidding from the evil, or else your evil ones would become office bearers upon you, then your good ones would be supplicating, but it would not be Answered for them’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Khalid from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Muhammad ibn ‘Umar ibn ‘Arafah who has said the following: “

I heard abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘You must ask (command) others to do good and prohibit them to commit evil, otherwise, the evil ones among you will be made your rulers and then the virtuous ones among you pray and their prayers will not be answered.’”
